title: Imagined speech EEG dataset — long words condition (Nguyen et al. 2017)
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 6 healthy participants performing imagined speech tasks with two conditions (cooperate and independent word imagery) using long words. The study employed a motor imagery paradigm with auditory and visual cues, yielding 3,600 preprocessed epochs (from 1,200 total trials, with 3 overlapping 2-second epochs per 5-second trial) recorded at 256 Hz from 64 channels. Data were analyzed using Riemannian manifold methods and relevance vector machines for brain-computer interface applications, achieving mean classification accuracy of 66.2±4.8%.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a BrainProducts ActiCHamp system at 256 Hz sampling rate from 64 channels (60 EEG, 4 EOG) using standard 10-20 montage. Participants performed imagined speech tasks cued by auditory beeps (5 beeps at 1.4s rhythm) and visual cues. Preprocessing included bandpass filtering (8-70 Hz, 5th order Butterworth), 60 Hz notch filtering, and adaptive EOG artifact removal. Each 5-second trial was split into 3 overlapping 2-second epochs.
